clue.text: 'People seen in church', paper reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like the paper term when spoken

blocks.note: a quire is a measure of paper, traditionally 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: A newspaper's report on who turns up at church services.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks fence off the definition, so 'paper reported' reads like a citation but is really the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of singers who perform at services are among the most visible people in any church building.

clue.text: Romp involving vacuous farce: a shocking movie

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word is emptied of its middle and only its outside letters remain
involving means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a caper is a playful escapade
outer letters of farce
taken as written

explanation.surface: A silly comedy caper turns out to be a startling film.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Fear is a 1962 thriller, remade by Martin Scorsese in 1991, famous for its menace.

clue.text: Old earl taking short sleep on toilet, making no effort

definitions.note: the answer is an adverbial phrase meaning without any effort required

indicators.note: taking means holding something in, so one pair of pieces surrounds the rest

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for earl
a nap is a brief sleep
lat is a shortening of latrine, a military toilet

explanation.surface: An aged aristocrat dozes off while sitting on the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the sleep before the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handed to you this way arrives ready-served, with nothing required of you to get it.

clue.text: Bloody dog – shouting, explosive – that’s seen next to lamb

blocks.note: blood is red
a cur is a mongrel dog
to rant is to shout angrily
jelly is slang for gelignite

explanation.surface: A vicious, noisy, volatile dog is kept away from the sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lamb' suggests a field of sheep, but it is the roast on the dinner plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fruit preserve is the traditional British accompaniment served beside roast meat from young sheep.

clue.text: ... world’s a stage ...

blocks.note: first meaning: our planet, the earth
second meaning: Shakespeare's playhouse on London's Bankside

explanation.walkthrough: The dots and wording quote Shakespeare's 'All the world's a stage' from As You Like It; fittingly, the answer is both the planet and his own theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet is commonly called the globe, and Shakespeare's company performed at the famous Southwark theatre bearing that name.

clue.text: Here, every athlete tussles – to begin with

definitions.text: Here, every athlete tussles – to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of each preceding word

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A description of a preliminary race where all the runners jostle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a qualifying round is where every athlete competes, early on.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary round of a race decides who goes through, and comes at the start of a contest.

clue.text: Shivering, I’m wet, short of time, so get lively, get lively!

indicators.note: shivering means trembling and shaking, so the letters are shaken into a new order
short of means lacking, and time is T, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first occurrence of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cold and soaked is urged to hurry up and get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'get lively' is fodder and the repeated one is the definition. Welly, short for wellington boot, is British slang for effort or force.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang phrase urges putting more effort or energy in, like a boot's hard kick.

clue.text: Many dogs taking a pee

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: poodles are a dog breed
pee is how the letter P is spelt out

explanation.surface: Lots of dogs stopping to relieve themselves on a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pee' is not a bodily function but the letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means a great quantity, lots and lots of something.

clue.text: Some theses, say, specifically?

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so only part of the following letters are used

blocks.note: found running through the end of theses, all of say and the start of specifically

explanation.surface: Giving examples of particular dissertations.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: theses are, for example, long pieces of academic writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Theses are extended academic compositions, specific instances of written discursive pieces.

clue.text: Foreign newspaper very into Milan fashion house

indicators.note: into says one item goes inside the other, placed within its letters

blocks.note: Prada is the luxury label founded in Milan
V is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A foreign paper that is utterly devoted to a particular Italian designer label.
explanation.definitionFit: Pravda was the official Soviet Communist Party daily, a famous Russian title published in Moscow.

clue.text: Sad vocal remixed with Gallic spirit

indicators.note: remixing a track rearranges its parts, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words are used as fodder

explanation.surface: A melancholy song gets a dance remix, with a French accent added.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvados is an apple brandy distilled in Normandy, so it is a French liquor.

clue.text: Captain and chief briefly advanced security protocol

blocks.note: Capt is the short form of captain
Ch is a short form of chief
A is a short form of advanced

explanation.surface: Senior officers on a ship ran through the safety procedures quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' tells you all three words are abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Websites use this challenge-response test to check that a visitor is human and not an automated bot.

clue.text: Collapse, ululating at first, before god in place on the Euphrates

indicators.note: at first points to only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to collapse is to fall down
opening letter of ululating
Jah is a name for God, notably in Rastafarianism

explanation.surface: Wailing mourners fall down before their deity at a holy site beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the first pieces ahead of the god.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallujah is an Iraqi city lying on the banks of that great Mesopotamian river.

clue.text: Novel where Scrooge gets jolly in the end

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter only of the word it follows

blocks.note: Dickens's Scrooge is the archetypal skinflint
last letter of jolly

explanation.surface: A book in which the famously mean Scrooge finally cheers up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for something new, but it names a book: Stephen King's thriller of that title.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen King's 1987 thriller about an obsessed fan carries this one-word title.

clue.text: Decorator to make a mark here, curling’s seen

definitions.note: the definition describes a place; it stands for a noun phrase meaning where the sport is played

blocks.note: an icer decorates cakes
to ink is to mark with ink

explanation.surface: A painter and decorator leaves his mark on a room where wallpaper is peeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorator' suggests a painter, but here it is someone who ices cakes, and 'curling' is the sport, not wallpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Curling is played on a frozen indoor surface, a skating venue with a sheet of ice.

clue.text: Study disparaging Bright Eyes singer?

blocks.note: Art Garfunkel had a UK number one with Bright Eyes, from the film Watership Down
disparaging remarks are criticism

explanation.surface: Someone is running down the singer of a famous rabbit song.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, criticism of Art is literally disparaging Art Garfunkel; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Evaluating paintings and other works is an academic discipline, a field of scholarly study.

clue.text: Actor who starred in Calamity Jane and Homeland?

blocks.note: Doris Day played the title role in the 1953 musical
Damian Lewis starred in the TV series Homeland

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a performer who appeared in both a classic musical and a spy drama.
explanation.walkthrough: No one actor starred in both; the two stars' surnames combine.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Day-Lewis is a three-time Oscar-winning film star, famous for intense method performances.

clue.text: Admitted being frustrated about part of Superman costume

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: fed up means frustrated and annoyed
the big S on the chest, spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: A superhero confessed he was annoyed with his outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The part of the costume is the S emblem, written as its letter name.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to own up or make a confession is to acknowledge the truth of something.

clue.text: Wild, Met opera? Hang about

indicators.note: letters that are about are scattered around, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: all the letters of these three words form the fodder

explanation.surface: An unruly night at the Metropolitan Opera, someone urging others to linger.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of control and causing destruction is the idiomatic sense of charging around violently.

clue.text: Top grade – excellent – in addition

blocks.note: A is the highest exam grade
swell is dated slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A school report: top marks, outstanding, and more besides.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean also or too, adding something further to what came before.

clue.text: Baffled by drunken noise of moody teenager

blocks.note: you've got me means you have baffled me
hic is a drunk's hiccup

explanation.surface: A parent puzzled by the slurred sounds coming from a sulky adolescent.
explanation.definitionFit: A goth is a youth subculture member dressed in black and given to gloom, so the adjective describes one.

clue.text: Funny jokes about parking in capital

indicators.note: something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters are made strange by rearranging
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Comedians cracking gags about trying to find a parking space in a city centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Skopje is the seat of government of North Macedonia, so it is that country's chief city.

clue.text: Those who are smart voiced opposition to Trump policy

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out loud, so we want words heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: Trump's flagship policy was a border wall with Mexico; opponents would say no to it

explanation.surface: Clever people speaking out against a US president's programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes people who think they are clever and act as if they have every fact.

clue.text: Sperm oil oddly seen in kind of pad

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in odd-numbered positions only

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Whale oil turns up, strangely, in some sort of cushioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' suggests something absorbent, but it is slang for a home; a semi is a semi-detached house, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pad is slang for a home, and a house sharing one wall with its neighbour is one type.

clue.text: Wanting leader, sheltered deposed king

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and the leader is the first letter, so that letter goes
something deposed is overthrown, so the letters are tipped into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dethroned monarch who led a protected life until his downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposed' sits beside 'king' as if describing him, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred the Unready was an Anglo-Saxon ruler of England around the year 1000.

clue.text: Scratched a Monet, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is judged by its spoken sound

blocks.note: the Impressionist painter's first name was Claude

explanation.surface: Someone damaged one of the Impressionist's paintings, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Monet' looks like a painting, but it means a person called Monet, giving the painter's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Raking with nails or talons is to dig into a surface, the past tense of a cat's action.

clue.text: Duly pick playfully in this activity?

definitions.text: Duly pick playfully in this activity?

indicators.note: doing something playfully means messing about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: all the letters of both words form the fodder

explanation.surface: A fairground game where you properly choose something in fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the activity is one where you pick at random, for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: This fete game involves pulling an unseen prize from a tub, so picking is the whole point.

clue.text: Everyman, they say, given drink, acts creepily

indicators.note: they say signals a word as it sounds when spoken, not as it is written

blocks.note: the setter Everyman would refer to himself as I
to sup is to drink in sips

explanation.surface: The setter, after a drink, behaves in a sinister way.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often clue themselves as I or ME; here the setter's own name stands for that pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogling someone lecherously, looking them over with obvious interest, is unpleasant, leering behaviour.
